posts.name: Perela
posts.cooked:
Hello,

I am posting because I have received two completely different explanations regarding the closure of my World of Warcraft account.

I want the community to see what happened during my account appeal, because I believe players deserve to know how these cases are being handled.

My World of Warcraft account, which I have used for nearly 15 years, was permanently closed for:

“Exploitative Activity: Unauthorized Cheat Programs (Hacks)”

I have never used hacks, bots, automation software, or any unauthorized program. I appealed because I genuinely believed this was a false detection.

What happened next is deeply concerning.

One Game Master upheld the closure based on concerns related to cheating or fair play. But another Game Master later gave me a completely different explanation, claiming that my account was involved, either directly or indirectly, in exchanging in-game property for real-world currency.

So which is it?

Was I supposedly using unauthorized software, or was I supposedly involved in RMT? These are two completely different accusations.

For the record, I have never bought or sold gold, items, accounts, boosts, or services for real-world money. I have also never used cheating or automation software.

I understand that Blizzard will not reveal its detection methods, and I am not asking them to do that. But after nearly 15 years of following the rules, I believe I deserve at least a consistent explanation for permanently losing my account.

If both appeals were genuinely reviewed against the account logs, how did two Game Masters reach completely different conclusions about what I allegedly did?

This makes me seriously question whether my appeals were properly investigated or simply answered with different templates.

I am sharing this because this could happen to any player. A permanent account closure should require clear evidence and a careful review—not contradictory accusations that leave the player with no meaningful way to defend themselves.

I am asking Blizzard to conduct a genuine manual review of the account activity and provide one clear, consistent reason for the closure.

If anyone else has received conflicting explanations during an appeal, please share your experience.

To view the image, `drive.google.com/file/d/1v7F029ppj7Sh-_frmWccB3HT6qtnbQ-p/view?usp=sharing`

Missramsey:

Your conclusion assumes that because the penalty was severe, the decision must therefore be correct. That is circular reasoning. The severity of a punishment is not proof of the underlying allegation.

Occam’s Razor: Usually the simplest explanation is usually the best, when you have multiple options.

And circular reasoning is that you take a theory. You apply only evidence, largely circumstantial, that supports your theory. Then using that evidence you claim that it proves your original theory.

I took your claim. That your account is being permanently suspended for things you never did and took no part in. I then look at what Blizzard has previously said regarding on account actions, and what they have done regarding account actions. I look at historical evidence of their procedures and policies. Then I weigh what is more likely.

A: Blizzard has mistakenly attached your account to severe behaviors resulting in your permanent account closure. Even after you appealed, and were responded to by two GM’s, who claimed to investigate the issue and found gave you two different instances they found of this behavior. These GM’s are both somehow mistaken, and also, them finding two reasons to apply the action, proves that they are either automated, or did not investigate at all.

B: Blizzard found evidence that your account took part in actions that warranted permanent account closure. And the two reasons given by the GM’s, although different, can directly be correlated to each other. And after appeal, they found that the account did take part in the actions and is to be closed.

Missramsey:

One GM said third-party programs; another said real-money trading. Those are materially different accusations.

You could be using third-party programs to engage in gold trading or RMT hypothetically, making both statements true.

I am choosing to decide that Blizzard’s action against you account is more likely to be the right one, over that they made a mistake and never investigated.

I dont want to completely discount your claim. Now, what could have potentially happened. You participated in a boosting service that was dirty. Meaning that if you were part of a community that uses 3rd party addons, to assign you to groups, to boost people, and the gold they sent you in the mail, came from stolen accounts or RMT. You could be part of a discord community, that uses an addon to make groups for carry services. You didnt intentionally break the rules. And you may not have known that using an addon to form groups, or be assigned to carry groups was against ToS. You may not have suspected that the boosting community you were taking a part of, was in fact dirty and using gold bought with RMT.
